title: Better Microcopy
content: Improve all UI text for clarity and user guidance. Button labels: use action verbs ("Save Changes", "Create Account", "Send Message" - not "Submit" or "OK"). Form labels: clear, concise field names. Placeholder text: helpful examples, not label repetition. Error messages: specific, actionable ("Email must include @" not "Invalid email"). Success messages: confirm what happened ("Profile updated successfully"). Empty states: helpful next steps, not just "No items". Loading text: contextual ("Loading your projects..."). Tooltips: explain features briefly. Confirmation dialogs: clear consequences. Link text: descriptive (not "Click here"). Use sentence case for buttons and labels. Keep tone consistent throughout.

variants.simple: Improve UI text with clear, actionable labels and messages.

variants.advanced: Improve all UI text for clarity, guidance, and consistent voice. Button labels: use specific action verbs ("Save Changes", "Create Account", "Send Message", "Add to Cart" - never generic "Submit", "OK", "Click Here"), include object when helpful ("Delete Project", "Copy Link"). Form labels: clear, concise field names (not "Enter your email address", just "Email"), use sentence case. Placeholder text: helpful examples ("jane@company.com", "Search products..."), never repeat label, disappears so don't rely on it. Error messages: specific problem + how to fix ("Email must include @ symbol", "Password needs at least 8 characters" - not "Invalid email", "Password error"), friendly tone without blame. Success messages: confirm what happened with specifics ("Profile updated", "Message sent to Sarah", "3 items added to cart"), brief celebration without overdoing it. Empty states: explain what would be here + how to add it ("No projects yet. Create your first project to get started." with CTA button), include illustration if appropriate. Loading text: contextual ("Loading your projects...", "Searching...", "Saving changes..."), not generic "Loading...". Tooltips: explain what feature does briefly (under 10 words), when to use it, keyboard shortcut if applicable. Confirmation dialogs: clear consequences ("Delete this project? This action cannot be undone." with "Delete Project" / "Cancel" buttons), avoid yes/no. Link text: describe destination ("View documentation", "Contact support" - never "Click here" or "Learn more"). Tone consistency: define voice (professional but friendly, casual, technical) and apply throughout. Capitalization: Sentence case for buttons and labels (not Title Case or ALL CAPS).

author: Ersin KOÇ
